name: IMPC (International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium)
scope: Systematic knockout mouse phenotyping: 9,605 phenotyped genes, 10,341 mutant lines, 111,664 phenotype calls (release 24.0).
mapping_methods: Mouse genes; human relevance through orthologs (Open Targets provides evidence_impc and mouse_phenotype).

quantitative.summary: Statistical significance and effect size per phenotype call.

coverage_limitations: Mouse, not human; ortholog mapping required
Homozygous knockouts mainly; hypomorphic and missense effects absent
known_omissions: Human phenotype of a human variant cannot be read directly from mouse knockouts

reuse_decision.rationale: Open Targets integrates IMPC as evidence_impc and mouse_phenotype with human ortholog mapping; fetch source tables only if gene-level mouse detail is needed.

status.notes: Release page and FTP listing readable.

mechanism_evidence.note: mouse knockout phenotype; orthology to the human gene is an inference
mouse knockout phenotype used as a proxy for loss-of-function tolerance

evidence_profile.biological_context: Knockout mouse lines phenotyped in a standardised pipeline. The genotype is an engineered knockout in one organism, and phenotype calls are made per procedure.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Direct measurement of phenotypes in knockout mice, with statistical phenotype calls and release-specific thresholds.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: Moderate for the gene's role in the mouse. It is not allele-specific, differences between mouse and human physiology limit transfer, and compensation by paralogs is not resolved.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Mouse phenotype terms. They support a human loss-of-function phenotype only when concordant with human genetics.
evidence_profile.absence_means: No phenotype call means none was detected in the procedures performed; screen breadth and genotype coverage vary, and lines that were not phenotyped or are lethal have no adult phenotype.
